tasks.short: Operate shared office equipment and coordinate repairs when it fails.

steps.what: Operate office equipment, including copiers, scanners and telephone handsets.
Inspect the fault and attempt permitted resets or consumable replacement.
Record the office-equipment fault and send asset details to the facilities team.
Approve a chargeable repair or replacement within the spending policy.
Contact the repair provider and arrange an authorized service visit.
Test repaired office equipment and report whether normal service has resumed.

tasks.design: Configure an asset-linked fault form and repair register in the {HELPDESK}, with spending approvals in the {WORKFLOW}. Approved requests populate service messages in the {EMAIL} and visit details in the {CALENDAR}; the assistant checks the booking before sending and physically tests the repair.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical work dominates. Asset details, service agreements and repair correspondence are often separated, making coordination awkward.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, approval rules and message templates can remove repeated administration. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting these existing capabilities.
tasks.still_hard: Someone must inspect equipment, replace consumables, arrange physical access and judge whether a repair worked. Providers may require telephone coordination.
tasks.human_edge: Recognizing a physical hazard, choosing a practical workaround and explaining disruption to colleagues.
tasks.altitude: The week still contains substantial hands-on support, with less repair chasing. Decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a repeat-fault review for shared equipment.
reach.learn: Asset histories, service coverage and how downtime informs repair-versus-replacement decisions.

evidence.claim: Asset-linked forms, approval rules and templated service requests are established deterministic patterns.
Physical operation and repair verification limit the share of this task that software can remove.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
The asset register and service agreements can be accessed by authorized support staff.
The scope excludes employee usage monitoring; no model loop is needed.
unknowns: Which equipment has remote fault reporting or support integrations?
Who may authorize charges and accept completed repairs?
How much time is physical operation versus repair coordination?
Which access approvals or consultation under national rules apply?
research_questions: Can the existing {HELPDESK} handle assets, approvals and service templates without custom code?
Which provider interfaces support a reliable service request and acknowledgement?
new_work: Maintain asset identifiers, provider contacts and approval limits.
Check generated service requests and handle failed delivery.
Close repair records after physical acceptance.

tasks.short: Maintain paper and electronic files, document indexes and routine attendance records.

steps.what: Collect correspondence, attendance returns and document updates from departmental mailboxes.
Scan paper records with office scanners and check that every page is legible.
Choose document categories, record identifiers and filing locations using the filing policy.

loop.input: Unstructured records that lack reliable metadata, plus the approved filing taxonomy.
loop.output: Suggested document category and record identifier with supporting source passages.
loop.check: Validate identifiers against known records and categories against the taxonomy; a person approves ambiguous classifications.
loop.stop: One classification pass per record; missing identifiers or uncertainty go to the filing exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules handle structured submissions, but varied correspondence does not consistently name its record or category.

steps.what: Enter document metadata, save the correct version and update the document index.
Update attendance records from authorized returns and refer discrepancies to the record owner.
Review missing records, access exceptions and files due for archival or disposal.

tasks.design: Configure controlled intake, versioning and retention queues in the {DOCS}, with a deterministic connector for authorized attendance updates in the {HCM}. A bounded classifier proposes metadata only where rules cannot identify a record; approved metadata drives filing, while access changes and disposal require the records owner's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents arrive in mixed formats with inconsistent names. Copying between the mailbox, document repository and employee records requires local knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing repository controls cover much of the work. Faster connector development and bounded text classification make the remaining gaps cheaper to address.
tasks.still_hard: Poor originals, conflicting attendance returns and unclear retention rules need people. GDPR access, purpose and retention requirements still apply; employee-record changes may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving disputed records and recognizing when a document needs restricted handling beyond its apparent category.

ambition.what: A departmental records-completeness check before scheduled audits.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time resolving missing evidence and preparing records-completeness reviews. A delegated remit could let them request corrections directly; access and disposal decisions stay with the records owner.

reach.task: Prepare a retention and disposition review.
reach.learn: Record series, retention triggers, legal holds and evidence of authorized disposal.

reach.task: Review departmental records readiness before an audit.
reach.learn: Sampling, completeness criteria and reporting exceptions without exposing unnecessary employee data.

evidence.claim: Structured metadata, version control and retention queues can be implemented with repository configuration and deterministic connectors.
Free-text classification needs validation; it should not independently determine access permissions or disposal.
Employee-record processing requires GDPR controls and assessment of applicable consultation duties under national rules.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
An approved filing taxonomy and retention schedule exist.
Attendance updates transfer authorized facts; they do not infer absence reasons or make employment decisions.
The access and consultation range covers implementation effort; external approval waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: What proportion of records still arrives on paper?
Which metadata and attendance fields already enter automatically?
Who approves classification exceptions, access changes and disposal?
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply?
Are retention schedules and legal holds maintained?
research_questions: Does the {DOCS} expose version-safe, auditable writes and duplicate detection?
Can the {HCM} validate imports without committing incomplete attendance updates?
How accurately can a classifier match a representative set of local records to the approved taxonomy?
new_work: Review uncertain classifications and missing identifiers.
Reconcile failed attendance imports with the HR administrator.
Maintain filing mappings, connector permissions and retention rules.
Sample filed records for accuracy and inappropriate access.

tasks.short: Triage shared mail, route requests and coordinate routine correspondence.

steps.what: Read incoming messages and attachments to identify requests and relevant records.

loop.input: New messages and permitted attachment text, with approved request types and routing rules.
loop.output: Request type, referenced record and suggested queue, with source passages.
loop.check: Check record identifiers and allowed queues; unknown senders, sensitive content and uncertain matches enter human review.
loop.stop: One pass per message with a capped attachment size; unreadable or uncertain items go to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender and subject rules handle predictable mail; varied free-text requests need limited reading.

steps.what: Judge significance, urgency and sensitive handling; identify authoritative information for replies.
Forward requests and attachments to responsible internal teams and record ownership.
Draft routine correspondence from approved information and earlier messages.

loop.input: The request, selected approved sources and an applicable reply template.
loop.output: A reply draft with factual claims linked to the supplied sources.
loop.check: Use templates directly where possible; otherwise validate names, dates and amounts and flag unsupported claims for the sender.
loop.stop: One draft per request; absent or conflicting source information produces an exception instead of an answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard replies, but varied questions require limited composition from approved facts.

steps.what: Check content, recipients and attachments, then send the reply.
Check outstanding requests and remind internal owners when responses are overdue.

tasks.design: Configure shared-mail rules in the {EMAIL} and an ownership register with reminders in the {WORKFLOW}. Small bounded loops classify unmatched requests and draft replies from approved material in the {DOCS}; the assistant judges significance and approves substantive outgoing replies before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Messages mix requests, background information and informal commitments. Ownership and authoritative answers are often implicit.
tasks.enabler_now: Rules and request registers can handle predictable flow, while bounded models can read unmatched text and prepare source-linked drafts. Faster implementation lowers the cost of connecting these parts.
tasks.still_hard: Urgency, organizational sensitivity and ambiguous commitments require context. Incorrect recipients or attachments can expose personal data, so GDPR controls must cover the complete message flow.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding why a message matters, deciding when to escalate and responding tactfully to an upset or influential correspondent.

ambition.what: A weekly unresolved-request briefing for the administrative services manager.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time forwarding and chasing, and more time resolving stalled requests. With delegated authority, they can escalate overdue work through an agreed route without gaining authority to make another team's commitments.

reach.task: Review recurring causes of delayed departmental responses.
reach.learn: Service ownership, escalation thresholds and distinguishing workload problems from unclear handoffs.

evidence.claim: Rules, ownership registers and reminders can handle predictable internal message routing without autonomous agents.
The departmental evaluation reported drafting time savings but also hallucinations and no evidence of higher productivity overall.
AI literacy duties apply; introducing staff monitoring or task allocation requires a separate assessment of the relevant AI Act provisions.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
The task concerns a departmental shared mailbox, not unrestricted access to personal mailboxes.
The model cannot send messages or choose unrestricted recipients.
Status reporting concerns requests, with no individual employee scoring.
unknowns: Which request types have stable owners and approved replies?
What proportion of correspondence needs sensitive handling or a substantive commitment?
Who can approve external replies and escalation routes?
Which mailbox permissions, retention rules and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can the existing {EMAIL} and {WORKFLOW} support ownership and reminders through configuration?
How often does triage miss a significant message in a representative historical sample?
Does source-linked drafting reduce total drafting and review time at acceptable quality?
new_work: Review uncertain triage results and significant messages.
Verify draft facts, recipients and attachments before sending.
Maintain routing directories, approved answers and escalation rules.
Investigate delivery failures and sample incorrect or missed routing.

tasks.short: Arrange appointments, send confirmations and manage changes.

steps.what: Read appointment requests and collect participants, purpose, duration and constraints.
Compare participant availability, room availability, working hours and travel buffers.
Agree a suitable time and resolve conflicts between participant priorities.
Create the appointment, reserve resources and send the calendar invitation.
Send practical appointment details and reminders to participants.
Process cancellations or changes and update participants and reserved resources.

tasks.design: Configure booking types, required intake fields, availability rules and reminders in the {CALENDAR}, using the {WORKFLOW} only for fields or approvals it cannot handle. Participants choose permitted slots; the assistant negotiates priority conflicts and obtains the appointment owner's approval for exceptions before invitations are sent through the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking rules and delegated calendar access were incomplete, while requests arrived with missing details. External availability still required repeated exchanges.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking configuration can cover routine appointments without a model. Faster implementation makes small intake and resource-booking gaps cheaper to close.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, inaccessible external calendars and last-minute changes still need coordination. Calendar titles and attendee details need appropriate GDPR access controls.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating whose commitment can move and handling changes without damaging relationships.

ambition.what: Self-service appointment booking for external participants outside office support hours.

tasks.altitude: Routine booking exchanges shrink, leaving more time for difficult coordination. The assistant gains no authority to move protected commitments; appointment owners retain priority decisions.

reach.task: Coordinate recurring project checkpoints across teams.
reach.learn: Decision dependencies, participant roles and how meeting timing affects delivery milestones.

evidence.claim: Booking types, availability rules and reminders are established configuration patterns for routine appointment scheduling.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can turn an email thread into a meeting invitation with an agenda.
The departmental evaluation found scheduling took longer, supporting a measured pilot rather than assumed gains from model assistance.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Standard requests move to structured booking intake; exceptional mail and telephone requests remain assisted.
Calendar permissions and booking policies permit automatic invitations for participant-selected slots.
The approval gate in conflict resolution applies to policy exceptions; ordinary slot selection needs no staff approval.
Only authorized changes update existing appointments; ambiguous changes enter assistant review.
unknowns: Which appointment types can use self-service booking?
Are resource calendars and travel buffers maintained?
Which participants lack accessible availability information?
Who can approve priority exceptions and changes affecting other participants?
What access approvals and consultation under national rules apply?
research_questions: Can the {CALENDAR} enforce resource capacity, buffers and cancellation rules without custom code?
Does a pilot reduce total assistant effort after including exceptions and participant support?
Can booking changes be authenticated without exposing other appointments?
new_work: Maintain booking types, buffers, instructions and delegated access.
Resolve priority conflicts and assist participants who cannot use self-service.
Review ambiguous changes and failed resource reservations.
Check appointment errors and total coordination effort during rollout.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving exceptions, maintaining reliable records and coordinating difficult handoffs. Physical support and sensitive communication remain substantial; additional escalation authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Support the facilities manager with repeat-fault reviews.
Prepare records-completeness reviews with file clerks and the administrative services manager.
Coordinate project checkpoints with a project management specialist.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, booking rules, approvals and reminders.
Validate records, identifiers and source-linked drafts.
Apply access, retention and GDPR requirements in daily administration.
Measure total task effort, including review and exception handling.
Negotiate priorities and escalate unresolved requests clearly.
role.ambitious_version: A departmental service coordinator who offers external appointment booking, prepares audit-readiness checks and turns unresolved requests into specific management decisions, within delegated authority.

job.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
